transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-08 15:00 UTC; Duration 46 min; Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivers (Novus CTO), Priya Singh (Novus Infra), Tom Hammond (Novus Product)

Summary (auto): quick sync on access + staging issues; runbook share; targeted canary.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check-in, I think we have about 45 minutes. Maya and I will run through the staging findings and then hand off action items.
00:12 Alex: Sounds good. We've got Priya and Tom here. We had a messy run overnight so keen to hear what's up.
00:18 Maya: Cool, I'll start with the KV cache observations. During the 3am run we saw around 18% of requests hit a cold path because the prefix cache wasn't warmed. There was also a fallback to the smaller quantized variant which spiked latency.
00:32 Priya: Uh huh. We noticed the same — CPU on the gateway went up and then some responses timed out. We also saw CORS failures from the front-end tester.
00:40 Jordan: Right — two buckets: first, the K-V cash (transcriber: KV cash) warm issue; second, the CORS header - our gateway is returning a slightly different origin header when the token is forwarded through your internal gateway.
00:57 Tom: Quick Q — is that something in Redwood Dedicated or a config on our side?
01:05 Maya: Likely config on the staging gateway. Redwood's runtime will accept the forwarded origin if the header is preserved. Our quick workaround is to add an allow-origin wildcard for the staging domain or to preserve the incoming Origin header at the proxy.
01:22 Alex: We prefer not to wildcard even in staging. Priya, can you add a rule to preserve headers?
01:28 Priya: I can. I want to understand the SSO flow too — the SAML handshake we tried seemed flaky, might be related.
01:35 Jordan: On SSO - we saw a 502 occasionally when the metadata wasn't parsed. That's usually due to a missing assertionConsumerURL in the SAML response from your IdP test account. Maya, did you capture logs?
01:44 Maya: Yes, uploaded a snippet to the shared drive (link: drive.redwood/novus/poc/logs). The error line shows assertion consumer mismatch and then a retry which succeeded. So intermittent.
01:58 Alex: We used a generic test user. We'll spin up a dedicated test account and share the SAML metadata.
02:05 Tom: Also on KMS — when we tried encrypting keys the first time the call failed with 403. Is that expected if the principle is wrong?
02:13 Jordan: Yes 403 typically means permission issue. We have a small checklist in the runbook we'll share: KMS key policy needs to include the service role and the customer-managed key alias needs to be present.
02:25 Priya: We'll give Maya access to our KMS role.
02:30 Maya: Great. On the KV fallback test — we set up a config to fall back to a 4-bit quantized model variant when the cache misses exceed 20%. That allowed throughput but latency jumped from ~70ms to ~400ms per request.
02:45 Alex: 400ms is too high for our interactive product. What's the levers we can tune?
02:52 Maya: Two levers: 1) warm your prefix cache (preload common prompts/contexts), 2) use the intermediate quantization profile we recommend (8-bit PAT rather than 4-bit) which cuts latency to ~120-150ms. There's also batching config if you accept a slight tail increase.
03:12 Tom: Are those changes that Priya can make on infra, or do you need us to change model pins?
03:20 Maya: Primarily infra and config. We can also pin to the 8-bit variant from our side but for the POC it's easiest if Novus preserves the kv-cache prefix population during staging.
03:31 Priya: How do we do that practically? Is there a script?
03:36 Jordan: Yes - we'll share a preload script as part of the runbook. It hits endpoints with the top 200 prompts to populate the cache.
03:43 Priya: Great.
03:47 
04:05 Maya: On CORS, the failing requests are all XHR preflight OPTIONS; the server response was missing Access-Control-Allow-Credentials on a handful of requests, so the browser blocks them.
04:18 Alex: That resonates. Our engineers made a change to the proxy last week that strips the credentials header when the origin isn't recognized.
04:25 Jordan: If you can preserve that header we should be good. In parallel, I can push a temporary routing rule to the staging route to add the header back for your domain.
04:36 Priya: We'll try preserving it. If not, please push the route.
04:41 Jordan: Noted.
04:45 
05:00 Tom: On the benchmarking — Jordan you mentioned a spreadsheet. Can we review last night's numbers now?
05:08 Jordan: Yep. Topline: 5k requests run, mean latency 85ms, p95 210ms, error rate 0.9% — most errors align with the SSO and CORS issues. When the fallback to 4-bit happened, p95 shot to 780ms.
05:26 Alex: Hmm. The spike is concerning. If we switch to 8-bit as Maya suggested, that looks acceptable.
05:33 Maya: I re-ran a short bench with 8-bit and got mean ~92ms and p95 ~160ms. We need to validate output quality but for many of Novus's prompts the output delta was acceptable. We can add a small eval set you define for the quality regression check.
05:50 Tom: We'll prepare a 50 prompt eval set.
05:54 Jordan: Great. Add that to the repo and Maya will run it against 8-bit and 4-bit and share diffs.
06:02 
06:20 Priya: Question on fallback — is it automatic? In other words, if cache miss spikes, will Redwood automatically route to quantized variant?
06:28 Maya: There's a policy: we can set an auto-fallback threshold per route. For the POC we recommended manual control while we tune. Auto-fallback is possible but we'd prefer a staged canary.
06:38 Jordan: We'll do a canary at 50% traffic once the SSO/KMS/CORS fixes are in place and after we validate the 8-bit profile against the eval set.
06:46 Alex: Sounds good.
06:50 
07:10 Tom: Anything else on infra readiness?
07:14 Priya: We need the exact service role ARN that Redwood wants to assume for KMS access; right now we gave a broad role and then tightened it down but want final details.
07:24 Jordan: I'll send the role ARN template in the runbook. Also include the exact IAM permissions list.
07:30 Priya: Also open a port question — is there any outbound IP allowlist we need?
07:36 Maya: For Private deployments, yes outbound ranges are needed. For Hosted/staging tests normally none, but for Novus's hybrid proxy we recommend whitelisting 3 IP ranges (listed in the doc).
07:47 Priya: We'll check those.
07:50 
08:10 Alex: A quick commercial Q — you mentioned Anthropic in the RFP — how do you compare on the SLOs?
08:17 Jordan: Briefly: Anthropic has good latency but limited model catalog; Vertex AI gives scale but can be pricier for low-latency cases. Redwood differentiates with the batching + caching recommendations and the dedicated options which let you pin hardware for consistent p95.
08:33 Alex: Okay thanks.
08:36 
09:00 Maya: Back to actionables — I'll provision a KV-cache fallback test in your staging and run a 500-request bench, then upload results to the spreadsheet.
09:10 Jordan: And I'll share the runbook and the preload script.
09:14 Priya: We'll create the SSO test account and send SAML metadata by Monday.
09:19 Tom: We'll finalize the eval set and acceptance criteria doc.
09:22 Jordan: Cool. Anything else?
09:25 Alex: One more small ask — can you include a short drill on how to revert to previous model pins if quality regresses during canary? We want a clear rollback playbook.
09:34 Maya: Absolutely. We'll add a rollback subsection to the runbook with API calls and console steps.
09:41 Jordan: I'll also schedule the canary proposal times for 2026-07-14 and ping calendar invites.
09:46 Priya: Perfect.
09:50 
10:05 Jordan: Recap: Jordan share runbook + perf sheet (due 7/10), Maya does KV bench + fallback setup (7/12), Priya creates SSO test user (7/11), Tom shares acceptance criteria (7/13). Canary targeted 7/14.
10:25 Alex: Thanks all — helpful sync.
10:28 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack and with the docs.
10:33 (call ends)
